sentences.text: This massive dinosaur is estimated to have reached a length of 25 meters.
Lü Junchang and colleagues first named the species in 2013.
Most of the original material was lost during construction, though one dorsal vertebra was reconstructed from fragments.
The preserved vertebrae are kept at the Ganzhou Museum of Natural History under catalog number GMNH F10001.
The animal is more closely related to Euhelopus than to other titanosauriforms based on shared characters.
A 2023 phylogenetic analysis recovered it as a basal titanosauriform.
It belongs to the unranked family Somphospondyli.
Gannansaurus lived during the late Upper Cretaceous, approximately between 72 and 66 million years ago.
